newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CITIC Pacific loan upped to HK$8.8 bln.
newsitem.headline: CITIC Pacific loan upped to HK$8.8 bln.

text.p: CITIC Pacific Ltd's HK$8 billion loan facility has been increased to HK$8.8 billion after being oversubscribed, one of the issue's coordinating banks said on Tuesday.

"The response from the senior arrangers and arrangers has been overwhelming and underwriting commitments, including the senior arrangers and arrangers, total well over HK$11.95 billion," J.P. Morgan Securities Asia said in a statement.
It did not give an exact total for the oversubscriptions.
The deal is in two tranches.

Tranche A for HK$5.5 billion is structured as a 24-month revolving credit converting to a term loan with a five-year maturity, and paying a margin of 45 basis points per annum over the Hong Kong interbank offered rate (HIBOR).
Tranche B is for HK$3.3 billion and is a seven-year loan paying an interest margin of 50 basis points per annum over HIBOR.
The five co-ordinating arrangers are Banque Nationale de Paris, Hong Kong branch, Chase Manhattan Asia, HSBC Investment Bank Asia, Hang Seng Bank and J.P. Morgan Securities Asia.

ABN AMRO Bank, Bank Nationale de Paris, Hong Kong branch, The Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Chase Manhattan Asia, CIBC CEF, Commerz (East Asia), Deutsche Bank AG, Hong Kong branch, Dresdner Bank, Fuji Bank, Hongkong Bank, Hang Seng Bank, The Industrial Bank of Japan, ING Bank, Hong Kong branch, J.P. Morgan Securities Asia, NatWest Markets, Paribas Asia, The Sakura Bank, Sumitomo Bank and Westdeutsche Landesbank.
Bank of Nova Scotia, Banque Indosuez, Credit Lyonnais, The Development Bank of Singapore, DG Bank, Hong Kong branch, The Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan and Sanwa Bank, Hong Kong branch.

Bankers said last month the loan was for working capital and to repay a short-term HK$12.5 billion bridging loan signed in February to help fund its HK$16.25 billion acquisition of 20 percent of China Light & Power Co Ltd.
